new_entities.name: Pre-exercise caffeine intake
new_entities.description: Caffeine consumed before exercise in ergogenic doses.

new_entities.name: One-repetition maximum strength
new_entities.description: Maximal dynamic strength assessed with a one-repetition maximum test.

edges.effect_quant: The best synthesis reports a small pooled benefit for maximal strength overall, with SMD 0.20 (95% CI 0.03 to 0.36), but individual 1RM studies range from no effect to only about 2.5 to 2.7% improvement in bench press.
edges.mechanism: Caffeine may improve maximal strength by increasing central drive and reducing the perception of effort, but single-repetition strength is less metabolically limited than endurance tasks. That means the physiology supports only a modest effect, and expectation or training status can easily influence whether a given study sees a benefit.
edges.summary: The literature supports at most a small benefit of pre-exercise caffeine on 1RM strength, and the direct trial evidence is not perfectly consistent. This is a good example of an edge that is probably real on average but too noisy to overstate for every lifter or every testing setup.
edges.caveats: The effect is more consistent for upper-body strength than lower-body strength, and some studies use caffeine-containing pre-workouts rather than pure caffeine. People expecting a dramatic jump in 1RM from caffeine alone are likely to be disappointed.
